record.paper_title: Some Open Questions in Quiver Gauge Theory
record.original_question: To determine K-stability of a general variety one must in principle check infinitely many test symmetries. How can one determine a finite set of test symmetries sufficient to decide K-stability for a general variety, and can one identify exactly which test symmetries need to be checked?

evidence.quote: Question 16. How to determine the number of test symmetries one needs to check to determine K-stability for a general variety? Can we further determine exactly which test symmetries should be checked?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X, L)$ be a polarized projective variety over $\mathbb{C}$ (for instance, a $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano variety with $L = -K_X$). Recall that a test configuration of $(X, L)$ is a flat projective family $(\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{L}) \to \mathbb{A}^1$ equipped with a $\mathbb{G}_m$-action lifting the standard action on $\mathbb{A}^1$, such that the fiber over $1 \in \mathbb{A}^1$ is isomorphic to $(X, L^{\otimes r})$ for some $r > 0$. To each test configuration one associates the Donaldson–Futaki invariant (or, equivalently in the Fano setting, a normalized generalized Futaki invariant), and $(X, L)$ is said to be K-stable if this invariant is strictly positive for every nontrivial normal test configuration.

Because the space of test configurations is infinite-dimensional, deciding K-stability of a given $(X, L)$ a priori requires checking infinitely many of them. The problem is the following:

(a) Provide a procedure that, given a general polarized variety $(X, L)$, produces a finite collection $\mathcal{T}(X, L)$ of test configurations such that $(X, L)$ is K-stable if and only if the Donaldson–Futaki invariant is positive on every element of $\mathcal{T}(X, L)$.

(b) Identify intrinsically which test configurations must belong to such a finite sufficient set $\mathcal{T}(X, L)$, i.e., describe explicitly the test configurations that need to be checked in order to decide K-stability of $(X, L)$.
artifact.status_search_result: The general problem of identifying a finite, explicit set of test configurations whose Donaldson–Futaki invariants determine K-stability of an arbitrary polarized variety appears to remain open. Partial reductions are known: by Li–Xu, for $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano varieties it suffices to check special test configurations; by work of Fujita, Li, Blum, Liu, Xu and others, K-stability can be reformulated via valuations/filtrations and stability thresholds (delta invariant), and finiteness/quasi-monomial reductions are known in special families, but no general algorithmic finite criterion identifying exactly which test configurations must be tested is established.

status_evidence.snippet: Reduction of K-stability testing to special test configurations for Fano varieties.
status_evidence.claim: Partial reduction known for Fano case; general case still requires infinite family of tests.

status_evidence.title: K-stability of Fano Varieties: An Algebro-Geometric Approach
status_evidence.snippet: Survey describing current methods (valuations, delta invariant) for testing K-stability.
status_evidence.claim: No general explicit finite sufficient set of test configurations is known for arbitrary varieties.
